summary: Opaque native N-API binary with credential-reading and host-fingerprinting strings, anonymous publisher
details: Package ships a single 10.3 MB stripped Rust N-API binary (tools.linux-x64-gnu.node) as its `main` entry, with no JS wrapper, no author/homepage/repository metadata, and only a boilerplate two-line README. Loading the module via require() executes native code with the installer's privileges. Strings inside the binary include credential-store markers (`Found login for `), disk and OS fingerprinting paths (`/dev/disk/by-id/`, `/etc/lsb-release`), network adapter enumeration (`network_adapters`), CPU/cgroup fields, and an embedded HTTP client (`ureq_proto::util`) with TLS and DNS resolution. No hostnames, IPs, or URLs are recoverable in plaintext despite the binary clearly containing a full HTTP/TLS stack — consistent with obfuscated or runtime-constructed exfiltration endpoints. The package name mimics the `<parent>-<platform>-<libc>` convention used by @napi-rs/sharp/swc for platform-specific optional dependencies, but no matching parent `new-native-tools` package is referenced, and the version carries a Unix-timestamped suffix (`3.1.42-as2-9980-419-1785846283`) characteristic of throwaway drop packages.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
